newsitem.title: LATVIA: Estonia resumes surge, other Baltic markets quiet.
newsitem.headline: Estonia resumes surge, other Baltic markets quiet.

text.p: Key first-half results failed significantly to stir the sleepy Latvian and Lithuanian markets this week while Estonia's bull-run resumed after a brief bout of profit-taking.
Dealers and analysts say the snail-paced response in Latvia and Lithuania to all but a few results reflects the low level of local liquidity and a lack of foreign institutional investors.
Markets in all three countries remain divorced from trends elsewhere and were unmoved by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's remarks that U.S. economic growth had moderated.
However, foreign interest in Estonia was boosted by the European Commission's announcement last week that it qualified for the first round of EU entry talks.
ESTONIA

Profit-taking early in the week put a lid on Estonia's surge but the prospect of revised profit forecasts for leading banking shares proved to be a red rag which investors could not resist charging at.
The Talse index rose to a record of 346.14 on Monday from 322.86 last Thursday before investors began reaping quick returns.
It fell to 338.49 by Wednesday's close but rallied again on Thursday to 343.81.
Wednesday also saw record turnover of 184.46 million kroons.
Dealers expect further gains ahead of upward profit forecast revisions by key banking shares, Hansapank, Hoiupank and Uhispank.
Things may cool off a bit then but July results could keep the market bubbling.
LATVIA
A spate of corporate results failed to really move the bearish Latvian market and turnover was sluggish for all but a couple of sessions.
The bourse index only gained slightly over the week, rising to 378.45 on Thursday from 376.95 the previous Thursday.
Jekabpils Sugar, a secondary list stock, was the only share whose price was buoyed by results.
Its interim after-tax profit of over 500,000 lats was way beyond anything the market expected. It jumped almost 14 percent to 66 santimes on Thursday.
Market leader Unibanka maintained its steady rally, rising to 3.25 lats on Thursday before slipping back to 3.19 lats on Friday morning.
Dealers expect it to fall further on Monday when the state auctions one million of its shares in the bank at a minimum price of 3.05 lats.
LITHUANIA
The bourse's official list index, which covers its five leading blue chips, inched up over the week to 950.15 points from 939.64 points the previous week.
The list has been rising slowly but steadily the past two weeks as investors seek the safety of its transparent and proven companies.
But considering the results which have rolled in from the companies on the list, the performance of its stocks has been disappointing.
Rokishkis Cheese announced on Monday that its half year profit surged to almost 9.5 million litas from 1.25 million in the same period in 1996.
Its price actually fell slightly after the result was announced before rising to 43 litas from 41.50 on Thursday.
Dealers expect it and other blue chips to post further gains but expect no surge. -- Riga newsroom +371 722 66 93
